experiment: three back-to-back 2000-unit in_process sleep reps with no drain barrier, 20-way, while sampling once a second how many task_run rows the server had persisted for those reps
first_drop_line: server-1  | 17:08:05.429 | WARNING | prefect.server.utilities.messaging.memory - Subscription queue is full, dropping message for topic='events' queue_size=10000 retry_queue_size=0
conclusion: The recorder persists task runs at roughly 30.5 per second while the flow process is competing for the box and about 59.4 per second once it has the box to itself. The in_process configuration produces them at about 150 units/s on the sleep body, two to five times faster. The broker's 10000-message queue absorbs the first burst, which is why the first one or two reps come out intact, but any run that sustains more than roughly 59.4 task runs/s fills the queue and the server begins discarding its own records. In this probe 1000 of 6000 task runs were never written, and the recorder needed 61.9s after the last rep finished to persist what it had kept.
